[Turn 6 USER]
e048	The team could support a public beta for eight weeks if we rotate office hours, but the senior maintainer will be on leave during the last three weeks.
e049	Priya says that is fine because it forces knowledge sharing.
e050	He says it turns his absence into an experiment other people did not choose.
e051	We can move the date, but then we miss a workshop where many potential users will be together.
e052	The workshop is a real learning opportunity, not only publicity.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e053	Launching into a known reduction in experienced support is a real risk, and calling it knowledge sharing does not assign the work.
e054	The workshop also offers unusually concentrated feedback.
e055	One compromise is to use the workshop as an announced hands-on preview and schedule the public beta after the maintainer returns.
e056	That preserves some learning while delaying open access, though contributors may reasonably see it as another preview and workshop participants may still form expectations.
[Turn 7 USER]
e057	I am leaning toward releasing an openly downloadable “workshop preview” with a fixed end date, office hours, and no compatibility promise, then deciding on the public beta after we review installation failures and the maintainer returns.
e058	I dislike inventing another label, and I know people can keep downloaded software after the date.
e059	But I also do not want to call it a public beta when our support capacity changes halfway through.
e060	I have not resolved whether citations should be allowed to reference the preview.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e061	The proposal makes the support window and decision point concrete, but your discomfort is justified: a new label cannot fully control how released software is used.
e062	Citation is the unresolved commitment because it can turn a temporary preview into a durable scholarly object.
e063	You could provide a citable project description without presenting the preview interface as stable, but researchers may still cite the software version they used.
e064	The plan can bound your promise; it cannot make public use temporary in every practical sense.

e039	We learned today that installation is easier than we thought for people using the common package manager, but one private lab had a staff engineer quietly solving problems for everyone.
e040	Their researchers reported a smooth experience because they never saw the setup work.
e041	That makes our private evidence look weaker.
e042	On the other hand, a volunteer wrote a new installer over the weekend and wants real users before polishing it.
e043	I cannot tell whether this argues for release or for another round of testing.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e044	It argues against treating the private labs as representative, but it does not choose the next step by itself.
e045	The new installer could change the support burden, and public use could test it under real conditions.
e046	A bounded installation test with people who lack staff engineering might answer that question faster than either a full beta or more internal polishing.
